message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_cloudtrail.global` passes `sns_topic_name` from `aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail-sns-topic`, but nothing orders it after `module.cloudtrail_baseline:resource.aws_sns_topic_policy.local-account-cloudtrail`, which is what grants `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` permission to publish to that topic. Creating the trail before the topic policy exists fails with an invalid / insufficient SNS-topic-policy error. The module's `depends_on` via `var.cloudtrail_depends_on` only covers the S3 bucket policy, not the topic policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`aws_cloudtrail.global` sets `sns_topic_name = aws_sns_topic.cloudtrail-sns-topic[0].arn`, so it waits for the topic but not for `aws_sns_topic_policy.local-account-cloudtrail`, which grants `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` permission to publish. CloudTrail validates that permission when the trail is created, so the trail can fail with an SNS authorization error unless the topic policy is applied first (the same class of ordering problem the module already handles for the S3 bucket policy via `cloudtrail_depends_on`).

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches the project as a Shared VPC service project but has no dependency on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services`. Attaching requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the service project, so the attach can race API activation. The mirror-image resource in the same file (`google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host`) does declare `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`; nothing in the service-project resource's `host_project`/`service_project` attributes can reference the enablement.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service` attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute Engine API to be enabled in the service project. It has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`, whereas its sibling host-project resources (`google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host`, and `...service_projects` transitively) explicitly declare that dependency. Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_organization_security_policy_association.attachment sets policy_id from var.firewall_policy_attachments (policy_id = each.value) rather than from google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy, so Terraform cannot infer that the association must be created after the policy. When an attachment references a policy created by this module, the apply may fail because the policy does not yet exist. The association should depend on google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy (e.g. explicit depends_on), since no clean data reference is available (attachment keys don't correspond to the policy map keys).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_compute_organization_security_policy_association.attachment` takes `policy_id` straight from `var.firewall_policy_attachments` (a plain string), while the hierarchical firewall policies it attaches are created in this same module by `google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy`. Because there is no attribute reference or `depends_on` between them, Terraform can create/associate the policy before the policy exists on a first apply (the provider's own example sets `policy_id = google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy.id`). The association should be ordered after the security policy — e.g. `policy_id = try(google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy[each.key].id, each.value)` so a module-created policy is referenced when the attachment key matches a policy key and externally supplied IDs still win otherwise, or a bare `depends_on = [google_compute_organization_security_policy.policy]`.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
props/aws:cloudwatchlogs references transform stanzas via `REPORT-...` string values only, so no dependency is inferred. The referenced transforms.conf stanzas should exist before this props.conf is applied.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
props stanza 'props/aws:cloudwatchlogs' wires REPORT-forgecicd_cloudwatchlogs_lambda_tenant_fields -> transform forgecicd_cloudwatchlogs_lambda_tenant_fields, but references it only by string in `variables`. There is no ordering dependency, so the props config can be applied before the transform exists. Add an implicit dependency on the transform.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`splunk_configs_conf.forgecicd_cloudwatchlogs` references the transform stanza `forgecicd_cloudwatchlogs_lambda_tenant_fields` by name in its `REPORT-forgecicd_cloudwatchlogs_lambda_tenant_fields` variable, but the graph records no dependency on `splunk_configs_conf.forgecicd_cloudwatchlogs_lambda_tenant_fields`. The props stanza should depend on the transform it references.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
The AKS cluster uses managed Azure AD RBAC, but there is no dependency ensuring null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature (which registers the AAD-V2 feature/provider) runs before azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks. Adding an explicit ordering is needed to avoid intermittent cluster creation failures.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
module.aks_clusters:resource.azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks enables Azure AD-managed RBAC (`role_based_access_control.azure_active_directory.managed = true`), which requires the "AAD-V2" preview feature of Microsoft.ContainerService to be registered first. That registration is performed by module.aks_clusters:resource.null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature (a ~30 minute az CLI loop), but nothing orders the cluster after it: the null_resource has no dependents and the cluster has no reference to it. Both will run in parallel and cluster creation can fail with a feature-not-registered error. Add `depends_on = [null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature]` to the AKS cluster.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`module.aks_clusters:resource.azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks` is created with a managed `identity` block and AKS-managed Azure AD RBAC, which requires the `AAD-V2` feature of `Microsoft.ContainerService` to be registered first. That registration is performed by `module.aks_clusters:resource.null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature` (including polling until the provider is registered, which can take ~30 minutes), but nothing orders the cluster after it, so on a fresh subscription the cluster creation fails. Add `depends_on = [null_resource.register_aks_msi_preview_feature]` to the `azurerm_kubernetes_cluster.aks` resource.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
delete_http_settings references a probe (HTTPSETTINGS is associated with a PROBE), so the HTTP settings must be destroyed before the probe. But delete_http_settings only depends on set_probe (the create-time resource), not delete_probe, so destroy order between delete_http_settings and delete_probe is undefined and the probe may be deleted while still referenced. The destroy-time dependency should be on delete_probe.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`null_resource.delete_http_settings` runs a destroy-time local-exec that deletes the backend HTTP settings, which reference health probes. In Azure Application Gateway a probe cannot be removed while an HTTP setting still references it, so during teardown the HTTP settings must be deleted first. The resource's `depends_on` lists `null_resource.set_probe` (a create-time resource that does nothing on destroy) instead of `null_resource.delete_probe`, so no destroy ordering is established and the probe may be deleted before the settings that reference it (its `on_failure = fail` would then abort the destroy). It should depend on `null_resource.delete_probe`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
delete_http_settings must run before the probe is removed (HTTP settings reference the probe via enable_probe/probe), but no dependency expresses that: its depends_on lists the create-time set_probe rather than the cleanup resource delete_probe. It should depend on delete_probe so the HTTP-settings cleanup is destroyed before the probe cleanup.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`:resource.google_folder_iam_audit_config.default` uses `folder = local.folder.name` but the graph shows no dependency on `:resource.google_folder.folder`. Data-access audit configuration can only be set on an existing folder; add `depends_on = [google_folder.folder]` to make the ordering explicit.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_folder_iam_audit_config.default sets folder = local.folder.name, which resolves to google_folder.folder via the local/conditional. The audit config can only be applied after the folder exists, but the dependency on google_folder.folder is not captured. Add an explicit depends_on on google_folder.folder.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_logging_project_exclusion.logging-exclusion creates a project-level log exclusion via the Cloud Logging API but has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services, unlike google_logging_project_sink.sink, so it can be applied before logging.googleapis.com is enabled.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_logging_project_exclusion.logging-exclusion` manages Logging exclusions against the Logging API but never waits for `google_project_service.project_services`. When `logging.googleapis.com` is enabled via this module, the exclusion can race the API activation. There is no attribute to reference here, so an explicit depends_on is the correct fix.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper` may be created, and the scheduled rule may fire, before `aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper` grants EventBridge permission to invoke the function; the target should be ordered after the invoke permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper can invoke aws_lambda_function.ssm_housekeeper only if aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper (principal events.amazonaws.com) exists first. The target references the rule and the function ARN but not the permission, so EventBridge may register the target before the invoke policy exists, causing scheduled invocations to fail. Add an explicit dependency on aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper points the scheduled rule at the ssm_housekeeper Lambda, but it does not depend on aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper, the resource-based policy that authorizes events.amazonaws.com to invoke the function. Once the rule+target exist (and the rule is ENABLED), an invocation can fire before the Lambda permission is created, causing invocation AccessDenied failures. The event target should be created after the Lambda permission.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels creates channels through the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on :resource.google_project_service.project_services. When monitoring.googleapis.com is being enabled by this same module, the channel create call can race API enablement (which is eventually consistent) and fail. Its downstream sibling google_monitoring_alert_policy depends on these channels, so the failure propagates. Add depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services].

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels` creates Cloud Monitoring notification channels but does not wait for `google_project_service.project_services`. When `monitoring.googleapis.com` is enabled via this module, channels can be created before the API is active. No attribute reference expresses this ordering; a bare depends_on is appropriate.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.elk references the `elastic-certificates` Secret by name in its chart values, but nothing orders it after kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates. Elasticsearch/Kibana pods can start before the TLS Secret exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`helm_release.elk` mounts the `elastic-certificates` secret (TLS certs for Elasticsearch) by literal name only, so no Terraform edge exists. The release should depend on `kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates` so the certs exist before the chart's pods start.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`helm_release.elk` mounts the Secret `elastic-certificates` (secretMounts in elasticsearch/kibana/filebeat/apm/metricbeat) by literal name, but does not depend on the `kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates` that creates it. Pods will fail to start if the Secret is absent, so the release must be ordered after the Secret.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the AWS VPC CNI `aws-node` DaemonSet, which must only happen once Calico has been installed and is providing pod networking. It currently depends only on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`/`module.eks`, so nothing orders it after `:resource.null_resource.create_calico_installation`; Terraform may delete `aws-node` before the Calico `Installation` exists, leaving the cluster without a working CNI. Add an explicit `depends_on = [null_resource.create_calico_installation]` (there is no clean attribute reference on a `null_resource` to express this).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
null_resource.delete_daemonset deletes the aws-node (VPC CNI) DaemonSet, which should only happen once Calico has been installed so a new CNI is in place. It currently depends only on module.eks and null_resource.update_kubeconfig, so nothing guarantees null_resource.create_calico_installation has run first — deleting the CNI beforehand leaves nodes without pod networking. Add a dependency on null_resource.create_calico_installation.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_daemonset deletes the aws-node (VPC CNI) daemonset, but it only depends on module.eks and null_resource.update_kubeconfig. It must be ordered after null_resource.create_calico_installation so the Calico CNI Installation exists before the previous CNI is torn down; otherwise nodes are left with no working network plugin and pods scheduled by later steps (Karpenter, node pools) will fail. No attribute of a null_resource gives a clean data reference, so an explicit depends_on = [null_resource.create_calico_installation] is the appropriate fix.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`:resource.google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` mutates the project IAM policy (cloudresourcemanager/IAM APIs) but is only ordered after `:resource.google_project.project`. `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` enables those APIs asynchronously and sets `disable_on_destroy`/`disable_dependent_services`, so on create the roles granted here may refer to services that are not yet enabled, and on destroy the policy binding is removed in parallel with the APIs being disabled — the same failure mode the module already guards against on `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`. It should depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` (bare `depends_on`; no attribute here can reference the service resources).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` only depends on `google_project.project` (via `project = google_project.project.project_id`); nothing orders it after `google_project_service.project_services`. Setting authoritative bindings requires the project's IAM/Cloud Resource Manager APIs to be live, and on destroy the module disables services (`disable_on_destroy = true`, `disable_dependent_services = true`), so removing bindings after the APIs are torn down fails. This is the same ordering the module already encodes for `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta` ("depend on services or it will fail on destroy"). Add `depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services]`.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` only references `google_project.project`, so it can be applied before the APIs in `var.services` are enabled. The members it binds often include service agents that are created only when their API is enabled (e.g. `<project_number>@cloudservices.gserviceaccount.com`), and disabling services on destroy with surviving bindings can error. It should depend on `:resource.google_project_service.project_services` (e.g. via depends_on, as already done for `google_compute_project_metadata_item.oslogin_meta`).

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`google_project_iam_member.additive` grants whatever roles are listed in `var.iam_additive_roles`, which can include the custom roles created by `google_project_iam_custom_role.roles` in this same module. A role cannot be granted before it exists, so the additive member must be ordered after the custom role. The sibling authoritative binding already expresses exactly this ordering with `depends_on = [google_project_iam_custom_role.roles]`, but the additive member relies only on input variables, so no implicit dependency exists and the two can race.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`:resource.google_project_iam_member.additive` builds its `role` argument directly from `var.iam_additive_roles`, which may contain ids of custom roles created by this same module (`google_project_iam_custom_role.roles` via `var.custom_roles`). Nothing in the code establishes ordering, so the additive bindings can be attempted before the custom role exists and fail (the module's own comment already notes additive roles "might fail due to dynamic values"). The authoritative counterpart `google_project_iam_binding.authoritative` explicitly orders itself after `google_project_iam_custom_role.roles` for exactly this reason; the additive members should do the same via `depends_on = [google_project_iam_custom_role.roles]`.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
:resource.google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts is created via the Cloud Monitoring API but only references notification channels implicitly; it never waits for :resource.google_project_service.project_services, so alert policies can fail when monitoring.googleapis.com is enabled in the same apply.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts` creates alert policies against the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on `google_project_service.project_services`. When `monitoring.googleapis.com` is enabled by this module, policy creation can race API activation. This is not expressible as a data reference, so an explicit depends_on is the fix.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch uses vpc_options (subnets + security groups) but has no dependency on aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch. Per AWS provider docs, the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch service-linked role must exist before a VPC domain can be created; when both are created together a depends_on from the domain to the role is required to order creation. Add an explicit depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
The VPC-based OpenSearch domain `:resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` uses vpc_options, which requires the AWS service-linked role for OpenSearch (`:resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch`) to already exist. Per the provider docs, the domain must be ordered after the `aws_iam_service_linked_role` (typically via `depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch]`). No attribute reference or depends_on expresses this today, so on a fresh apply the domain can fail with "service-linked role not found".

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The VPC-based OpenSearch domain requires the AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService service-linked role to already exist, otherwise the first `terraform apply` fails with "You must create the service-linked role for Amazon ES". The example defines `aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch` (gated by `var.create_iam_service_linked_role`) precisely for this, but `aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` never references it and has no `depends_on`, so nothing orders the role before the domain. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch]` on the domain.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
null_resource.delete_http_listener does not depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port. HTTP listeners reference the frontend port, so on destroy the listener must be removed before the frontend port. delete_http_listener currently lists null_resource.set_frontend_port instead — a create-only resource with no destroy provisioner — leaving delete_frontend_port with no incoming ordering, so the port may be deleted while a listener still references it. delete_http_listener should depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
delete_http_listener depends on create-time set_frontend_port, which has no destroy provisioner, rather than on delete_frontend_port. The listener references the frontend port, so during teardown delete_http_listener must run before delete_frontend_port.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_http_listener has a destroy-time provisioner that removes an HTTP listener which references a frontend port. The frontend port cannot be removed until after the listener is gone, so delete_http_listener must be destroyed before delete_frontend_port. It currently depends_on null_resource.set_frontend_port (a create-only resource with no destroy provisioner), which does not order the actual frontend-port deletion. It should depend on null_resource.delete_frontend_port.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer creates a vpc_config from var.lambda_subnet_ids/var.lambda_security_group_ids but is not ordered against module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role; both depend only on aws_iam_role.syncer_lambda and the subnet inputs. A VPC-attached function whose execution role lacks ENI permissions fails to create, so an explicit depends_on is required.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.syncer uses a vpc_config but only references aws_iam_role.syncer_lambda; it never depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role. Lambda creation will fail if the role lacks AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole at that moment, so the function must be ordered after the VPC execution-role attachment (e.g. via depends_on).

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`aws_cloudtrail.main` only references `aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail` (via `s3_bucket_name`), so nothing in the graph forces `aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail` to be applied first. CloudTrail validates that it can write to the target bucket at creation time and fails with `InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException` if the trail bucket policy (AWSCloudTrailAclCheck / AWSCloudTrailWrite) is not already attached — an ordering gap that is worse on a fresh apply where the bucket is brand new. The provider's own example documents `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example]` on the trail for exactly this reason.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_cloudtrail.main only references aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail.id, so nothing forces aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail to exist before the trail is created. CloudTrail validates the bucket policy (s3:GetBucketAcl / s3:PutObject for cloudtrail.amazonaws.com) during CreateTrail and fails with InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException if the policy isn't attached yet. The AWS provider docs for aws_cloudtrail explicitly show `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example]` on the trail; add `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail]` to aws_cloudtrail.main (no attribute-level fix exists, since aws_s3_bucket_policy exports no attributes).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.aws_cloudtrail.main` only references `aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail` (via `s3_bucket_name = aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail.id`), which orders it after the bucket but not after `:resource.aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail`. CloudTrail validates S3 access when the trail is created and will fail with `InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException` unless the bucket policy granting `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` s3:GetBucketAcl / s3:PutObject is already applied (the provider's own `aws_cloudtrail` example uses `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example]` for exactly this reason). Since the trail performs no attribute reference on the policy, the graph contains no edge and the two are applied concurrently.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_eks_node_group.this` only orders against `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role.this` (through `node_role_arn`); it has no dependency on `module.eks_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this`. The node role ARN exists before the AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy / AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly / CNI policies are attached to it, so Terraform may create the node group (and EKS start launching and joining instances) while the role is still permissionless, and on destroy the role can be stripped of permissions before EKS has finished terminating instances and ENIs. The AWS provider documentation for `aws_eks_node_group` explicitly recommends depending on the role policy attachments for exactly this reason. The launch template's own `depends_on` only covers the case where this module creates the launch template.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
The EKS managed node group (aws_eks_node_group.this) only references the bare IAM role (node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.this[0].arn) and has no dependency on the role's policy attachments. Per the official aws_eks_node_group docs, the node group must be created after (and destroyed before) its AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy / AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly / CNI policy attachments exist, or nodes fail to register and EKS cannot cleanly delete instances and ENIs. No attribute reference or depends_on expresses this ordering.

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
aws_scheduler_schedule.pool points target.role_arn at aws_iam_role.scheduler.arn and therefore waits for the role, but the lambda:InvokeFunction permission the target actually needs is in the separate inline policy aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler, which no edge orders before the schedule. Because the schedule uses flexible_time_window mode = "OFF" (an exact, immediately-active schedule_expression), the first fire can happen while the execution role still has no invoke permission, and the pool is never resized until the next scheduled run. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler] to aws_scheduler_schedule.pool.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
aws_scheduler_schedule.pool triggers aws_lambda_function.pool using aws_iam_role.scheduler, but it only references the role's ARN. The permission that actually lets that role invoke the Lambda (lambda:InvokeFunction) lives in aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler, a sibling resource attached in parallel. Because IAM inline policies are eventually consistent, Terraform can create the schedule before the role is authorized, so the schedule's first invocation can fail with an authorization error. The schedule should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler (e.g. depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler]); there is no attribute on the schedule that can carry this reference.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
aws_scheduler_schedule.pool targets aws_lambda_function.pool with role_arn = aws_iam_role.scheduler.arn, but it does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler, the inline policy that actually grants the scheduler role lambda:InvokeFunction. The policy is only ordered after data.aws_iam_policy_document.scheduler (which needs the function ARN), so it can be created after the schedule.
